subject: PayGrid model fit eval — follow-up & parity thresholds
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks + next steps on PayGrid model fit eval

Alex — great to meet today, really appreciate the time and clarity on PayGrid's core failure modes. Quick recap and proposed next steps:

- Goal: validate whether an open model + prompt set can meet/beat your current proprietary baseline on intent classification and entity extraction for refunds and charge disputes.
- Success criteria you mentioned: 95%+ intent accuracy on production-weighted traffic; tolerance for drift of <=2% absolute on primary metric for parity.

Next steps we committed to:
1) Share our initial prompt set and the evaluation harness (attached).
2) Run a baseline evaluation: Llama-3-70B-8k-quant, Falcon-Refined-40B, and Redwood-Proprietary-3.1 on your sample set.
3) Share results and recommended path (prompt tuning vs quantization adjustments vs model swap).

I've attached the prompt-set-v1.txt and an initial CSV schema for results. Marissa will run the first pass and share a summary by early next week. If anything above is off, flag it and we'll adjust.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Mobile: (415) 555-0199

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@paygrid.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks + next steps on PayGrid model fit eval

Thanks Lauren — that matches our read. A few clarifications from the product side:

- When we say 95% intent accuracy that's weighted by our weekly traffic distribution (refunds are ~60% of calls here). For entity extraction we care more about exact-match on the refund_reason field.
- Parity threshold: our legal/comms team wants "no meaningful regression" defined as <=1.5% absolute drop on intent accuracy or <=2% drop on refund_reason exact-match. We can be flexible if you can show tangible latency or cost benefits.

Practical asks:
- Can you run the baseline eval against a 10k record sample (we can provide S3 access).
- Please include 95th percentile latency numbers for each model (cold and warmed KV cache) — latency is a hard requirement for user experience.

Priya (CC) will share S3 paths. Looking forward to the results.

—Alex
Director of Product, PayGrid
alex.turner@paygrid.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@paygrid.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks + next steps on PayGrid model fit eval — initial run attached

Alex / Lauren — we completed the first-pass eval against the 1k stratified sample PayGrid shared last week. Key items attached: paygrid-eval-results.csv and a short evaluation dashboard link (also attached as a txt link). Highlights:

- Models tested: Llama-3-70B-8k-quant, Falcon-Refined-40B, Redwood-Proprietary-3.1 (v3.1-2026-02).
- Primary metric (intent_accuracy): Redwood-3.1 = 96.8%, Llama-3-70B = 95.4%, Falcon-Refined = 94.9%.
- refund_reason exact-match: Redwood-3.1 = 92.1%, Llama-3-70B = 90.5%, Falcon-Refined = 89.8%.
- 95th pctl latency (warmed KV cache, single-request path): Redwood-3.1 = 210ms, Llama-3.1-70B = 280ms, Falcon-Refined = 240ms.

Interpretation: on this 1k sample the open Llama variant is within ~1.4% absolute on intent_accuracy vs your proprietary baseline — that sits near the band you and Priya described. refund_reason exact-match is ~1.6% delta.

Notes and quality concerns:
- We see a small cluster of failure modes where the open models hallucinate rare merchant codes — we included examples in the CSV (column: failure_case_comments).
- Prompt sensitivity: a few intent failures were resolved by small prompt adjustments (see prompt-set-v1.txt lines 12-22). We recommend a controlled prompt-tuning pass before declaring parity.
- Cost/latency tradeoff: Llama-3-70B quantized delivers cost benefits but needs additional prompt and temperature tuning to tighten exact-match.

Next recommended steps:
1) Run the full 10k sample you offered (we can pull from S3 link).
2) Run a prompt-tuning sweep for Llama-3-70B limited to the top 10 prompt variants we noted and re-evaluate.
3) Produce a parity decision matrix (accuracy vs latency vs cost) for your stakeholders.

I'll schedule a short technical review to walk through the CSV and failure examples. Lauren — want me to include kernel/serving config notes (quantization, KV cache warm-up) in that session?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@paygrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PayGrid eval — logistics for 10k run and tuning

Alex — thanks for the S3 offer. A couple quick logistics items to confirm before we kick the 10k pass:

- Sample format: expect JSONL with fields {"text","intent_label","refund_reason"}. If you have any additional metadata (customer_tier) please include it so we can weight results.
- Access: please grant read-only to infra@redwood-evals.svc account; we'll only read the sample and not persist sensitive payloads beyond evaluation window.
- Infra: for the 10k pass we can run on our hosted infra; no Dedicated infra required unless you'd like a lower-latency SLA test. If you want to validate under Dedicated conditions we can schedule a short Dedicated node spin-up (cost estimate attached in Drive link).
- Timeline: we can complete the 10k baseline + 10 prompt-tuning runs within 4 business days after we have S3 access.

Marissa — please confirm the exact kernel/quantization config you used in the 1k pass so Alex can match expectations.

- Aditya
Technical Product Manager | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@paygrid.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@paygrid.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PayGrid eval — logistics for 10k run and tuning

Thanks team — I've shared the S3 path and a read-only role with the infra account you specified. S3: s3://paygrid-eval-samples/round1/10k.jsonl

We're good with you running on hosted infra for the baseline, and will request a Dedicated run if the initial parity looks promising. Timebox the prompt-tuning to the top 10 variants you suggested.

Acceptance check: if after tuning Llama-3-70B is within <=1.5% absolute intent_accuracy and <=2% exact-match refund_reason vs Redwood-Proprietary-3.1 AND latency at 95th pctl is within 1.3x of Redwood-3.1, we'll consider moving to a longer proof-of-concept.

Please confirm once you start the 10k pass and send a calendar invite for the technical review — Priya and I will join.

—Alex
Director of Product, PayGrid
alex.turner@paygrid.com
